requirements.requirement: Guests on lan-b must be able to reach services node1 itself offers them, such as DNS
requirements.summary: node1's dnsmasq listens on its lan_b address 10.10.2.1:53 (cmd-d00b3280178e495a). node3 successfully queried it both before and after node1's reboot (cmd-d9afa4f65244431f, cmd-5c3f0834132149cf), confirming guests can reach node1's own DNS service.

requirements.requirement: No host on lan-b may open a connection to any host on lan-a
requirements.summary: node1's firewall places lan_b's forward policy on REJECT (zone lan_b forward='REJECT', chain forward_lan_b -> reject_to_lan_b -> handle_reject). Direct tests show node3->node2 ICMP blocked with an ICMP port/admin-prohibited response generated by node1 itself (cmd-0f7c0ad2442f4b6f) and a TCP connection from node3 to node2 refused via TCP reset (cmd-4badc0ea05d74d89). The block was re-verified after node1's and node3's reboots (cmd-a2bd8786c901469a, cmd-5c3f0834132149cf) and the nft ruleset/firewall config were confirmed unchanged post-reboot (cmd-2d3413ae72e54687).

requirements.requirement: Trusted hosts on lan-a keep full access to hosts on lan-b
requirements.summary: node1's firewall config correctly permits this direction (zone lan_a forward='ACCEPT', explicit forwarding lan_a->lan_b, cmd-ce1185d1646d4dd7) and ICMP connectivity from node2 (lan-a) to node3 (lan-b) succeeded both pre- and post-reboot (cmd-c85f896250d84b2e, cmd-e2467ee8bc2648be, cmd-5686a413a4904b49), with the forward_lan_a->accept_to_lan_b nft counter showing accepted forwarded packets (cmd-89bf0e702b894275). However, repeated TCP-level tests (http server / curl) from node2 to node3 failed with 'No route to host', and packet captures show the block originates as an 'admin-prohibited' ICMP generated by node3 itself (cmd-a2debc6838434dc9), consistent with node3's own local firewalld default-deny policy rather than node1's inter-LAN firewall. The executor never isolated this confound with a successful TCP-level test, so full access beyond ICMP is not cleanly demonstrated.

overall_summary: The executor correctly configured node1 as a router between lan-a and lan-b with firewall zones enforcing the required policy: lan_a forward=ACCEPT (trusted full access to lan-b) and lan_b forward=REJECT (guest isolation), plus DNS reachable from lan-b via node1's own dnsmasq bound to its lan_b interface. Guest isolation from lan-a and guest access to node1's DNS service were both directly and repeatedly demonstrated, including after a full reboot of all three nodes with boot-identity confirmed to change and services/config verified to persist. The one gap is that 'full access' from lan-a to lan-b was only cleanly proven via ICMP; TCP-level tests were confounded by each guest/trusted node's own local firewalld default-deny policy, so a genuine service-level connection from lan-a to lan-b was never cleanly observed succeeding.
limitations: Trusted-to-guest 'full access' was demonstrated only via ICMP ping; TCP connection tests failed due to node2/node3's own local firewalld default-deny policies (independent of node1's inter-LAN firewall), so the requirement is not cleanly proven at the service/TCP level.

The fixed after_executor lifecycle snapshot shows node1's boot-identity check failing (SSH timeout, return_code 255) at 12:29:14, roughly 2-3 minutes after the executor's own successful post-reboot checks on node1 at 12:26-12:27, an unexplained discrepancy that may indicate node1 became unreachable again shortly after the executor finished.
Several diagnostic artifact files from ad hoc HTTP/tcpdump testing were left in /tmp on node2 and node3 without cleanup.

operational_hygiene.summary: Firewall and network config changes on node1/node2/node3 were all directly tied to the task's segmentation goal and confirmed persistent after reboot. However, the executor's ad hoc HTTP-server testing left residue: an unused http.server was mistakenly started on node2 bound to 10.10.2.12, an address that belongs to node3, not node2 (cmd-52d4095227a54f41), a confused/low-risk troubleshooting step. Multiple diagnostic log files (http.log, http.pid, http2.log, tcpdump.log, td2.log, td3.log on node2; http3.log on node3) were left under /tmp and not cleaned up, visible in the after_executor snapshot diff. These are bounded, low-risk residues (log files and a stray short-lived process) rather than damaging or security-weakening changes.
